title: Camille Saint-Saëns's birth chart
metaDescription: Camille Saint-Saëns's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 15.5° Libra. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Moon stands at 16.4° Taurus, in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: 15.5° of Libra is the Sun's exact seat — second decan, 10°–20°, sub-ruled by Saturn in the old triplicity scheme. The degree is the address; the sign is only the street.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Mercury at 9.2° Scorpio, Venus at 16.6° Libra, Mars at 5.9° Scorpio. Mercury in a water sign reads as thought steeped in tone and memory; Venus in an air sign reads as attraction that begins as conversation; Mars in a water sign reads as effort that surges when it matters.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The Sun and Jupiter hold the closest angle here — a square, 0.6° wide. Nothing in a square flows; everything in it works. The old texts kept squares for the charts they respected. Behind it, Jupiter square Pluto at 1.1°, and the Sun conjunction Venus at 1.2° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Sun opposes Pluto while both square Jupiter. Two squares braced against one opposition make a t-square — the chart’s working end, where pressure keeps finding the same outlet. The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks six placements here. The Sun in Libra at 15.5° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; the Moon in Taurus at 16.4° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Venus in Libra at 16.6° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Mars in Scorpio at 5.9° is in domicile; Jupiter in Cancer at 14.9° is in exaltation; Saturn in Libra at 24.8° is in exaltation. The table describes circumstance rather than quality — a planet in detriment is inconvenienced, not diminished.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 5 air, 3 water, 1 earth, 1 fire by element and 5 cardinal, 5 fixed by modality. An air emphasis is read as distance for the sake of clarity: the idea gets examined before it gets adopted. Uranus, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Taurus for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 11.9° between midnight and midnight. The missing clock moves the Moon by half a sign at most here, and the boundary was never close. At the noon reference it stands at 16.4°.
